** ἡσῠχ-ιος**,

2287:
** θᾰνᾰτήφορ-ος**, ον,
**death-bringing**, αἶσα {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 369 (Lyric poetry)}}; περίοδος θ. cycle **of mortality**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 617d}}; of hurts or accidents, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 48}}; of a surgical operation, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Antyllus Medicus cited in 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 45.17.6}}; ῥίζα ἐν Αἰθιοπία, of arrow-poison, **Acokanthera Schimperi**, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 9.15.2; ὀδύναι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Partibus Animalium” 672a36}}; γένεθλα.. θ. κεῖται **causing death by contagion**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 181 (Lyric poetry)}}; πᾶσαι μεταβολαὶ πολιτειῶν θ. {{LXX+5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.3.32; ἁμαρτία LXX.Num.18.22}}; δίκαι **capital** trials, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|“Not.Arch.” 4.19 (Cyrene, Aug.); ἐπιστολή 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 4.12.8; περιστάσεις 2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 225.7}}. _adverb_ -ρως, νοσεῖν {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 2.148S.}}: _neuter_ _singular_ as _adverb_, ἐπλήγη οὐχὶ -φόρον {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aeneas Tacticus 27.9}}; but -φόρον ᾄδειν to sing **a death song,** {{Refs 1st c.AD+|Anthologia Graeca 11.186 (1st c.AD: Nicarchus Epigrammaticus).}}
2290:
** θάπτω**,
_future_ θάψω {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 8.21}}:—_passive_, _future_ τᾰφήσομαι {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 632, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.45, also τεθάψομαι 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 577, 1141, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1464}}: _aorist 1_ ἐθάφθην {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Simonides Lyricus 167 (conjecture), 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.81, 7.228}}; more frequently _aorist 2_ ἐτάφην [ᾰ] {{Refs|[prev. author] 3.10, 55}}, and alwaysin _Attic dialect_, as {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 556}}; _participle_ ἐν-θαφείς {{Refs|“CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 2839 (from Aphrodisias):}}_perfect_ τέθαμμαι, _Ionic dialect3rd.pers._ _plural_ τετάφαται variant{τεθάφαται} {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 6.103; _imperative_ τεθάφθω 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “DMar.” 9.1}}; _infinitive_ τεθάφθαι {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 366 (Lyric poetry, probable reading), 4th c.BC: Lycurgus Orator 113}}: _pluperfect_ _passive_ ἐτέθαπτο {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.52, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.113}}:—**honour with funeral rites**, ὅτε μιν θάπτωσιν Ἀχαιοί {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.323, compare 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 472; especially by burial, οὐ γάρ πω ἐτέθαπτο ὑπὸ χθονός 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 11.52}} (but frequently used later with _reference_ to cremation, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 3.55, 2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Ἀννιβαϊκή” 35, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Heroicus” 10.11, etc.; πυρὶ θάπτειν 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.286f, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Vitae Sophistarum” 2.20.3); θάπτειν.. γῆς φίλαις κατασκαφαῖς 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 1013, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 545 (_passive_)}}; θ. ἐς χῶρον {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.41; οὗ ἐβούλοντο 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.84}}; θ. ἐξ οἰκίας **to carry out to burial** from a house, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 8.21}}; καταλείψει μηδὲ ταφῆναι not even his **burial expenses**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 556; τῷ δ᾽ εἶναι μηδὲ ταφῆναι [prev. author] “Ec.” 592.}}
